facts.statement: Titan is a framework-neutral work-kit compiler with PHP as its only runtime dependency.
A compiled work kit names outcome, first action, dependencies, scope fence, selected Quain capability identities, verification steps, completion criteria, and failure criteria.
CodeAction, PlanCommit, PlanPr, PlanOption, and Checkin enter Titan as portable adapter DTOs that preserve Landing source identifiers and provenance.
Dependency-incomplete work can be assembled but cannot be presented as executable or dispatchable.
Plan option selection and checkin recording are explicit transitions and are not inferred from timestamps or UI state.
Logres owns current execution after dispatch; Titan does not own runtime or current-state.

assumptions.statement: Hosts will map existing Landing Eloquent rows onto the portable DTOs until catalogue extraction tickets land.
Empty dependency sets are complete and therefore executable when the rest of the contract is present.
When no plan options are supplied, the CodeAction intent is a sufficient outcome for compilation.

decisions.decision: Selected capabilities are Quain identities only.
decisions.rationale: Titan must not duplicate capability semantics.

decisions.decision: Compilation accepts assembled kits when dependencies are incomplete and refuses executable presentation.
decisions.rationale: The contract can be named for inspection without becoming dispatchable.

decisions.decision: Changing a selected option requires dismiss then select.
decisions.rationale: Lifecycle must stay explicit and testable.

decisions.decision: Catalogue persistence, task graphs, interrupts, and repository bindings stay on child tickets.
decisions.rationale: MME-1211 is the compile contract, not the rest of Titan.

constraints: Titan does not depend on Laravel, Eloquent, HTTP, queues, Blade, NativePHP, or provider SDKs.
Titan does not own UI rendering or provider-specific execution.
Titan does not compute Logres runtime readiness.
Public package consumers must not require licenses or private dependencies.

open_questions.question: Which exact Landing columns survive catalogue extraction versus remaining host-only?
How should MME-1226 attach a planned-task graph to an already compiled work kit without rewriting this contract?

glossary.definition: The compiled, presentation-neutral description of intended executable work.
A compiled kit that names the contract but is not dependency-complete.
A compiled kit whose declared dependencies are satisfied and that may be presented for dispatch.
Eloquent, UI, or mixed-ownership behavior that remains in Landing until a child ticket extracts it.

features.name: Compile planning records into executable work kits
